title: Gratin de courgettes
subtitle: Provençal courgette gratin with eggs and Gruyère
excerpt: Sliced courgettes baked with eggs, crème fraîche, Gruyère, and garlic into a set, golden gratin. A summer staple from the south of France, equally at home as a side dish or a light main.
sourceNotes: Gratin de courgettes is a classic Provençal vegetable preparation widely documented in French regional cookbooks. Zucchini/courgette gratins appear throughout the culinary literature of Provence, the Languedoc, and the Rhône Valley. The method of setting a vegetable gratin with eggs and cream is standard in the French culinary tradition.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be assembled up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerated unbaked. Bake from cold; add 5 to 10 minutes to the cooking time.

content.text: This gratin is a Provençal summer constant: simple to make, flexible about timing, and good both hot and at room temperature. The courgettes are salted first to draw out moisture, which prevents the gratin from being watery. The egg-and-cream custard sets around them as they bake, the Gruyère browns on top, and the result is firm enough to cut into portions.

items.prepNote: for drawing moisture from the courgettes

content.text: Put the sliced courgettes in a colander, toss with the salt, and leave for 30 minutes to draw out moisture. Rinse, then pat very dry with kitchen paper or a clean cloth.

Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C). Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the courgettes in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per batch, until lightly golden on each side. Do not crowd the pan. Transfer to a large baking dish.

Whisk together the eggs, crème fraîche, garlic, thyme, and three quarters of the Gruyère. Season with pepper (the courgettes will already be salty from the salting). Pour over the courgettes. Scatter the remaining Gruyère over the top.
Bake for 40 to 50 minutes until the top is deep golden and the custard is set in the centre. A knife inserted in the middle should come out clean. Leave to rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

items.cause: Courgettes not salted and dried before cooking
items.fix: Always salt courgettes and pat them dry. If it has already happened, pour off the excess liquid and continue baking until the custard sets.

items.cause: Gratin dish too deep, or oven temperature too low
items.fix: Cover the top with foil if it is browning too fast, and continue baking.

content.text: Gratin de courgettes is the sort of recipe that every family in Provence makes in August when the courgettes are too many and too large and need to be dealt with. It is served at room temperature at lunch, reheated for dinner, packed in the cool-bag for a picnic. It works as a side dish beside grilled fish or lamb, or as a main course with a salad.
